problem: WRONG TARGET. The spec maps "Your spells... that deal fire damage gain a status bonus to damage equal to half the spell's rank" to targetKind 'spell'. In this app 'spell' is not a generic spellcasting bucket — src/rules/explain.ts defines it as `{ kind: 'spell'; entryId: string; which: 'dc' | 'attack' }`, i.e. the Spell DC and spell-attack-modifier tiles. Burn It grants NO bonus to spell attack rolls or spell DCs; it boosts the damage the spell deals. Starring the Spell DC / spell attack stat with a damage bonus is exactly the mis-target the brief warns about, and a player reading it would think their attack roll or DC went up.
correction: Keep situational:true and needsEngineWork:true but return ZERO bonuses. All three clauses are damage OUTPUT, which has no target kind: (a) spell fire damage (+half the spell's rank, min +1), (b) alchemical-item fire damage (+one-quarter the item's level, min +1), (c) +1 status to persistent fire damage. engineNote should say the missing capability is a spell-/item-damage-output target, not that one clause maps to 'spell'.

problem: Wrong target. The +1 circumstance bonus is to a kineticist IMPULSE attack roll, and the spec files it under targetKind 'spell' (the spell attack/DC statistic). A kineticist is not a spellcaster and has no spell attack statistic on the sheet, so the star would either never render or — worse, on a dual-class or archetype caster — mark a spell attack the feat never touches. AoN's Kineticist class entry (aon-2e-archive by-category/class/class-23.json) settles it: "Your impulse attack roll uses the same proficiency and attribute modifier as your kineticist class DC... Like a spell attack modifier, your impulse attack modifier uses the following formula" — it is only *like* a spell attack, it IS the class-DC statistic (Con + class DC proficiency, the same track derive.ts uses for Elemental Blast).
correction: Keep situational: true and the condition text ('on the Magnetic Pinions impulse attack roll against a target wearing metal armor or made of metal'). Change targetKind from 'spell' to 'classDc' — the closest legal kind and the statistic the roll is actually built from — and set needsEngineWork: true with the note that an impulse ATTACK ROLL is not the class DC itself (it is that statistic minus 10) and there is no impulse-attack target kind; the same gap affects every kineticist impulse-attack feat. The needsHumanDecision question should be restated as 'should impulse attack rolls get their own target kind, or ride classDc?' rather than 'is spell the right bucket?', which is answered: no.

problem: The condition is invented and mis-attributed. The record says: "When you Treat a Disease or a Poison, or someone else uses one of these actions on you, increase the circumstance bonus granted on a success to +4". The spec's `when` reads "...or someone with this feat treats you" — the text imposes NO requirement that the treater have the feat (the feat is yours; any treater's success gives you +4). The other half is also wrong on your own sheet: when YOU Treat a Disease/Poison on an ally, the improved +2→+4 goes to the PATIENT, not to you, so "after you Treat a Disease/Poison" should not appear as a condition on your own save unless you treated yourself. Confirmed identical wording in the AoN mirror (feat-5207.json / feat-836.json).

Add an engineNote: when you use Treat a Disease/Poison on an ALLY, the improved bonus lands on the ally and is not representable; the success→critical success upgrade is a degree-of-success change with no representation.

problem: WRONG TARGET / sign inversion. problem: The condition is broader than the rules allow. problem: The needsHumanDecision question states the bonus is "+1 or +2, higher with a tower shield". That is wrong: core.json gives tower-shield acBonus 2, identical to steel-shield (buckler is 1). problem: The needsHumanDecision question offers "attach it to the splendid psychopomp mask item record once the item lane is wired up" as if that were a safe deferral. problem: The +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves is ALREADY folded into the computed total by the engine, so a feat-keyed situational entry double-reports it. core.json stances['cobra-stance'] carries saves.fortitude {value:1,type:'circumstance'}, and derive.ts:172-173 reads it ("The active stance/form may grant a save bonus (Cobra Stance: +1 Fortitude), typed so it pools") whenever the stance is active. problem: Mis-shaped as a registry entry. problem: The condition is narrower than the text. core.json reads "Your first attack that hits a frightened creature after you roar and before the end of your next turn gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage" — ANY frightened creature. problem: The classification (unconditional, belongs in the maths) is right, but needsEngineWork:false is wrong. A `saves` grant field on feats (parallel to the existing `speeds` field, 72 feats) is needed before 'it belongs in the maths' is true."

problem: The classification (ally's AC, nothing to star) is correct, but the engineNote misstates the data. It claims 'guardians-deflection' has "no level field" — the record has "level": 4. problem: Wrong bonus magnitude in the parenthetical. The spec writes the bonus as "+your raised shield's circumstance bonus (usually +1; +2 for a tower shield)", which inverts the actual shield values. core.json: items/buckler acBonus 1, items/steel-shield acBonus 2, items/tower-shield acBonus 2. The +1 case is the buckler (the uncommon case); +2 is the normal shield, tower shields included. The feat itself says only "you gain your shield's circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects that would deal void damage" — it names no numbers, so the parenthetical is the reviewer's gloss and it will be read at the table as "+1" by most shield users who actually get +2.

Change the bonus string to "+your raised shield's circumstance bonus (+2 for most shields, +1 for a buckler)". problem: Wrong target on the second bonus. The feat grants "a status bonus to damage" for spells cast from slots — it is a SPELL DAMAGE bonus. The spec maps it to targetKind 'spell', which in this registry is the spellcasting attack roll / spell DC stat, and then admits in engineNote that this is 'a best-effort mapping'. correction: Drop the targetKind 'spell' entry entirely. Keep the strikeDamage entry ("+status equal to your number of weapon damage dice", for 3 rounds, vs undead / creatures holding an imprisoned soul / creatures you have witnessed create or command undead — note core.json says 'witnessed', not 'seen'). Keep needsEngineWork true, with the note now reading: spell DAMAGE has no target kind in the list (the 'spell' kind is the spellcasting attack/DC), so this half cannot be marked until a spell-damage marker or a Spells-tab display exists; also the whole package can be redirected to a willing creature in the spiral's light, which the registry cannot express.

problem: The bonus ladder is incomplete and starts too high. The feat's first effect is "Add Lastwall soup to your list of herbal items" — at 4th level the holder makes BASE Lastwall soup, which items/lastwall-soup gives as "a +2 item bonus to Stealth checks and DCs against undead". Secondary: the bonus is to "Stealth checks and DCs against undead" and only the check half is captured — the DC half is the same DC gap flagged on other records, but it is not mentioned here.
correction: Both human-decision questions are CONFIRMED and should stay: (a) the feat by itself grants nothing until soup is eaten, and (b) the +3/+4 conflict is real — feats/gravelands-herbalist says Greater grants "+4 item bonus" while items/lastwall-soup-greater's own text says "+3 item bonus" (and still calls itself 'improved Lastwall soup', so that record looks like a copy-paste of the Improved entry). Fix the emitted bonus to the full ladder: "+2 item (base soup), +3 at 10th (Improved), +4 at 18th (Greater, per the feat; the item record says +3)", when: "for 1 hour after you eat Lastwall soup, to Stealth checks and DCs against undead". Add to the engine note that the 'and DCs' half has no target kind.

problem: Inconsistent DC handling, and needsHumanDecision is wrongly false. The +4 circumstance bonus is to your Deception DC (what observers roll Perception against), not to any Deception check — the spec says so itself and still emits a skill/deception marker. problem: Not an error in the spec, but it will be dropped as a duplicate if applied blindly: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts ALREADY contains a numb entry, and that existing entry is wrong — it reads bonus "+1 circumstance (+2 while your body is destroyed)". problem: Structurally broken: situational is true but the spec carries NO bonuses array at all (only needsEngineWork + engineNote). Nothing on this character's own sheet changes.' problem: Condition broadened. The spec's when reads '...to determine whether it is disguised or transformed'. The record grants the +2 only for the disguise case: 'When you actively Seek a creature within range of your scent, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Perception check to determine if it's disguised.' As written the spec tells the player the +2 applies to a check it does not apply to.
correction: when: 'on your Perception check to determine if a creature is disguised, when you actively Seek it within range of your scent'. problem: Condition dropped. Bonus string '+1 circumstance (+2 if you critically succeeded at the Tumble Through)', targetKind skill/deception and situational:true are all correct against the text.

problem: needsEngineWork:false contradicts its own engineNote ('when the ally is the target the bonus belongs on their sheet, which the app cannot show') and is inconsistent with how the same self-or-ally structure was flagged elsewhere in this batch — known-weaknesses, connect-the-dots, clue-them-all-in and lead-investigator all set needsEngineWork:true for exactly the missing 'bonus conferred on another character' lane. problem: The mechanics in the spec are right (+2 circumstance on the Investigate / Recall Knowledge check when you lick or taste, skill 'all'), but the spec treats this as a NEW entry and never notices that src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts ALREADY has a supertaster key — and the existing one is a misread: `"supertaster": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'perception' }], when: "Perception to detect alterations/additives in food or drink you consume", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }]`. problem: Spec is presented as a new authoring, but shadowplay is already in the registry with the same content: `"shadowplay": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'acrobatics' }], when: "Tumble Through the opponent's space after a damaging melee Strike", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }]`. If you want the spec's slightly fuller phrasing, edit the existing entry's `when` in place to "on the Acrobatics check to Tumble Through with Shadowplay (requires your last action was a melee Strike that damaged that opponent)" — do not add a second key.

problem: The lore skill key is wrong. The spec uses target skill `lore:bardic-lore`. The app's canonical lore key is `lore:<subject>` with the word "Lore" STRIPPED — `loreKey()` in src/builder/shared.tsx:3061-3068 does `.replace(/\blore\b/g, '')`, so "Bardic Lore" canonicalises to `lore:bardic`. correction: Use skill `lore:bardic`. Keep needsEngineWork:true, but only for the real gap: the entry must be gated on the character also having the `bardic-lore` feat (core.json feats['bardic-lore'] exists), and the registry has no second-feat predicate. problem: The condition is broadened — it drops the tradition restriction from the BONUS and states it only on the trigger. Spellmaster's Resilience (core.json, verified) gives "+1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells and effects with that tradition's trait"; Tenacity only says "increase the circumstance bonus to saving throws from the Spellmaster's Resilience feat to +2". correction: Re-word the `when` to carry the tradition restriction on the bonus itself and mark it as a replacement: { targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'all' }], when: "against spells and effects of your chosen tradition, for 1 minute after this reaction (once per day, when you critically fail such a save)", bonus: "+2 circumstance (replaces Spellmaster's Resilience's +1; its resistance also rises to 10)" }. problem: The Disable target is narrowed beyond what the record says. The text is "a +2 circumstance bonus ... to checks to Disable magical traps" — it names no skill. The spec assigns skill `thievery` with confidence "high" and needsHumanDecision:false. Magical traps routinely publish Disable entries for Arcana / Nature / Occultism / Religion (and the trap's own listed skill) as well as Thievery, so a Thievery-only star under-reports — and it is inconsistent with the same engineer's own sure-foot call, where an unnamed skill was deliberately given detail 'all' to avoid over-narrowing.

problem: The engineNote's list of panache-granting skills is factually wrong. It says "Acrobatics / Athletics / Deception / Diplomacy / Intimidation". Verified against core.json classFeatures: battledancer = Performance, braggart = Intimidation, fencer = Deception, gymnast = Athletics, rascal = Thievery (Dirty Trick), wit = Diplomacy (Bon Mot). So Performance and Thievery are missing, and Acrobatics is not a style skill at all — Acrobatics comes from Tumble Through, which the `panache` class feature grants the bravado trait for EVERY swashbuckler, and which the spec already covers in its own separate entry. Anyone using that note to narrow the target later would silently drop two styles.
correction: Fix the note to: styles are Performance (battledancer), Intimidation (braggart), Deception (fencer), Athletics (gymnast), Thievery (rascal), Diplomacy (wit); Acrobatics is the universal Tumble Through clause, not a style. Also set needsEngineWork:true — the app DOES know the chosen style (classFeatures battledancer/braggart/fencer/gymnast/rascal/wit), so narrowing skill 'all' to the one style skill is a real, doable engine improvement rather than a hypothetical. The three bonuses' sizes, types and the qualifying-condition list (clumsy, drained, enfeebled, frightened, sickened, stupefied) are confirmed correct.

problem: The save is broadened to 'all'. The record says the bonus applies "on their ongoing saves against poisons already present in their body". Poison is an affliction, and PF2e affliction/poison ongoing saves are Fortitude saves; there is no poison that calls for an ongoing Reflex or Will save. Starring Reflex and Will with "against poisons" tells a player at the table to add +2 to rolls that will never happen. The spec's stated reason ("to avoid over-narrowing") is also the opposite of the call it made on glyph-expert, where an unnamed skill was narrowed to one.
correction: Use save 'fortitude': { targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'fortitude' }], when: "for 1 minute, on ongoing saves against poisons already in the body when you cast cleanse cuisine on the creature (you or a touched ally)", bonus: "+2 status" }. Keep needsEngineWork:true for the correct reason the spec gave — the spell can be cast on a touched ally, so the bonus may land on someone else.

problem: Invented condition. The spec's 'when' reads "an enemy just succeeded at against you", but the record's trigger is unqualified: "**Trigger** An enemy makes a successful Disarm, Escape, Grapple, Shove, or Trip attempt." Nothing in the text requires the maneuver be aimed at the character — by RAW an enemy Grappling an ally triggers it too. The displayed condition would make a player wrongly decline the reaction.

problem: Wrong target for the only bonus emitted. Mind Mace reads "You gain a status bonus to mental damage with spells you cast equal to the spell's rank" — that is spell DAMAGE, but the spec files it under targetKind 'spell', which in the sheet is the spell attack/DC line. The spec's own engineNote concedes it "may render on the wrong number", yet still emits it, so the star would land on a stat the feat never touches. Secondarily, the engineNote's blanket claim that "there is no initiative stat in the list" overstates the gap: the existing registry already files initiative bonuses under perception (e.g. 'all-this-has-happened-before' — "on your initiative roll (once per day)"; 'ambush-awareness' — "on Perception checks rolled for initiative").
correction: Emit NO bonus entry for this record. Set situational false/needsEngineWork true with the note: spell-damage has no target kind (only strikeDamage exists), Psychic Fist is an attribute substitution, and the +2 circumstance to psychic-duel initiative can only be filed under 'perception' IF duel initiative is a Perception roll — core.json's rules/psychic-duels record is empty (id + name only), so that is unverifiable from the data. Keep the human-decision question about duel-only bonuses.

problem: Condition narrowed. The text has two clauses: "a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to reposition or shove you. This bonus ALSO applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to force you to move." The second clause names no save type, but the spec folds it into the Fortitude and Reflex entries only, so a Will save against a forced-movement effect would show no marker.

problem: Wrong target: narrowed to save/fortitude on a bonus the text never restricts to a save type. The record reads "granting a +1 item bonus to saves and DCs against attempts to grapple or swallow you" — "saves" is unqualified, so any save prompted by a grapple/swallow attempt (e.g. a Reflex save against an effect that grabs you) qualifies. Foundry's own rule element for this item confirms it: selector ["saving-throw","fortitude-dc","reflex-dc","will-dc"], i.e. ALL saves plus all three DCs, predicated on action:grapple / action:swallow-whole. The spec's engineNote also contradicts its own choice: it states the practically important half is the Fortitude DC (which the player never rolls), then anchors the marker on the Fortitude save row — so the one row that gets a star is the roll least likely to happen, and Reflex/Will get no marker at all.
correction: Keep situational:true, +1 item, but set targetKind save with save:'all' (the registry's existing convention, as used by affliction-resistance / adaptive-vision). when: "against attempts to Grapple or Swallow you (the same bonus also applies to your Fortitude, Reflex and Will DCs against those attempts)". Leave needsEngineWork:true for the DC half (no save-DC target kind exists) and the needsHumanDecision question as written.

problem: The condition is narrowed beyond the text. Both bonus entries say the +2 applies "if the creature fails its save against your DC", but the record grants it on the creature's SUCCESS as well: "**Success** ... If your AC is being targeted, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC. If you need to attempt a saving throw, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the save." Only a Critical Success denies the bonus ("The spell or ability affects you normally"); on a Critical Failure the effect fails outright so no bonus is needed. As written the spec tells a player they get nothing on the enemy's success, which is wrong half the time.
correction: Reword both 'when' strings to cover success and failure, e.g. "against the triggering single-target spell or ability, unless the creature critically succeeds at its save against your class or spell DC (spend a Mythic Point)". Keep the engineNote's separate point that the crit-downgrade rider only happens on the creature's failure — that part is correct.

problem: Wrong target set: the four enumerated skills (arcana/nature/occultism/religion) do not cover the printed scope. The record says "You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to all primary checks to perform a ritual" — unrestricted. Checking core.json's `ritualPrimary` field across all 151 ritual records, 28 of them (18.5%) name NO tradition skill at all: e.g. clone -> "Crafting (legendary)", seed-of-mercy -> "Medicine (expert)", wild-allegiance -> "Diplomacy (expert)", power-of-the-beasts -> "Athletics (expert)", the-unseeing-blade-master -> "Perception (master)", halt-death -> "Warfare Lore (legendary)", bonding-meal -> "Cooking Lore, Crafting, Performance, or Survival (trained)", band-of-heroes -> "Diplomacy (mythic) or Society (mythic)". So roughly one ritual in five would show no marker. The engineNote's "a handful of rituals" understates this by an order of magnitude, and it is inconsistent with the same author's use of skill 'all' for Recall Knowledge (instructive-strike, willing-runes), which is a NARROWER set of skills than ritual primary checks.
correction: Replace the four entries with a single entry: { bonus: '+2 circumstance', when: 'on the primary check to perform a ritual', targetKind: 'skill', skill: 'all' }. (One ritual's primary check is even literally 'any' — unfettered-mark -> "Crafting (master) or any (legendary)".) Note that Perception is also a legal primary check for the-unseeing-blade-master, so a perception entry is defensible too if the app owner wants full coverage.

problem: The mapping is right but the needsHumanDecision flag is unwarranted and would block shipping four correct stars. The record reads "For the next 10 minutes, you gain a +2 status bonus to checks made using Acrobatics, Occultism, Stealth, or Survival" — this is the standard PF2e enumerating construction ('checks made using any of these'), not a choose-one. Nothing in the text offers a choice: there is no 'choose one', no 'one of the following', and the duration is a flat 10 minutes rather than per-check. Compare the genuine choose-one wording used elsewhere in the same data ('choose any skill you believe they are trained or better in' — borrowed-ability).
correction: Drop needsHumanDecision/question, raise confidence to high, keep the four skill entries (acrobatics, occultism, stealth, survival) exactly as specified.

problem: WRONG TARGET (wrong save). The spec splits the "saving throws to resist these actions" half as Fortitude = resist a Grapple, Reflex = resist a Disarm, Shove or Trip. Shove is resisted with the Fortitude DC, not Reflex — verified in core.json: actions.shove says "Attempt an Athletics check against your target's Fortitude DC", actions.grapple likewise Fortitude, while actions.trip and actions.disarm both say Reflex DC. A player following the spec would look for the star on the wrong defence half the time.
correction: Keep the +1 circumstance Athletics entry (when: 'to Disarm, Grapple, Shove or Trip, while your divine spark is in this ikon'), but re-split the resist half: save/fortitude — 'to resist a Grapple or a Shove, while your divine spark is in this ikon'; save/reflex — 'to resist a Disarm or a Trip, while your divine spark is in this ikon'. The spec's own needsHumanDecision (phrase it as a bonus to your Fortitude/Reflex DC rather than to the saves) still stands and is worth asking.

problem: INVENTED THIRD ENTRY / DUPLICATE STAR. The record grants exactly two bonuses: "You and your allies in the lantern's aura gain a +1 status bonus to visual Perception checks to notice anything that is also within the aura and a +1 status bonus to checks to Recall Knowledge against creatures within the aura". The spec lists a THIRD bonus, targetKind 'perception', when: 'granted to allies in the aura as well (same two conditions)'. There is no third bonus — that is the same aura benefit re-stated from the allies' side, and because it is filed under targetKind 'perception' it would render a second, condition-less-looking star on the CHARACTER's own Perception.
correction: Delete the third entry outright (not 'drop it if…'). Two entries only: +1 status / perception / 'visual Perception checks to notice something inside your lit lantern's 20-foot aura', and +1 status / skill:all / 'to Recall Knowledge about a creature inside your lit lantern's aura'. Mention the ally-sharing in the engineNote as prose only.

problem: FALSE needsEngineWork. The spec says the record's "you gain a +3 circumstance bonus to your initiative roll" (from "While holding your tome, you can always roll a skill check for initiative against creatures or haunts using Esoteric Lore") "has no target kind — the app has no initiative stat". That is not true of this registry: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts already carries initiative bonuses on the stat that is actually rolled — e.g. 'harmlessly-cute': skill/deception, when "when you roll Deception for initiative", and seven perception-based initiative entries (ambush-awareness, swaggering-initiative, proximity-alert…). Here the roll is an Esoteric Lore skill check, and lore keys are supported (SituationalTarget documents `lore:*`; build.ts trains classes.thaumaturge.trainedSkills.lore === 'esoteric' as `lore:esoteric`).
correction: Add a third entry instead of the engine flag: bonus '+3 circumstance', targetKind 'skill', skill 'lore:esoteric', when 'when you roll Esoteric Lore for initiative against creatures or haunts, while holding your tome'. Keep needsEngineWork only for the genuinely unrepresentable part (nothing left here, so it can be dropped).

problem: CONDITION MIS-STATED (trigger dropped, and wrongly framed as an optional pick). The record's cell reads "Impulse Junction Fragments of stone float around you, granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn" — the spec renders the condition as "if you took the earth impulse junction: until the start of your next turn after you use it", which (a) omits the actual trigger and (b) implies the junction is always a chosen extra. core.json classFeatures['kinetic-gate'] Single Gate says: "you gain an impulse junction, a benefit that occurs when you use an impulse of the chosen element that takes 2 actions or more … You can gain only one impulse junction per round" — so a single-gate earth kineticist has it automatically, and it only fires on a 2+ action earth impulse, once per round. As written a player would read the star as a standing AC bonus.
correction: Reword the AC entry's `when` to the printed trigger: 'when you use an earth impulse that takes 2 or more actions (once per round) — lasts until the start of your next turn'. Note in engineNote that Single Gate grants the element's impulse junction automatically, while dual/multi-gate characters choose it, so the 'if you took it' caveat applies only to the chosen case. The Athletics skill-junction entry is correct as written (the +1/+2 at 10th/+3 at 17th ladder is verbatim from classFeatures['gate-junction']).

problem: The PASSIVE half is marked situational (a star on strikeAttack), which contradicts this same engineer's own — and correct — reasoning on armored-skirt. Record text: "While wearing this ring, you add your level to your attack rolls with all weapons with which you are untrained." That is gated on the WEAPON'S PROFICIENCY, which is character data the sheet already knows, exactly like armored-skirt's "which armor is equipped" (rejected there as "not a table-time condition"). It is also not a typed bonus at all — it substitutes level into the untrained proficiency math. Worse in practice: the shipped SituationalTarget has no per-weapon granularity ('attack' is global), so this star would render on EVERY strike, telling a fighter who is trained/expert in the weapon they're holding that they get a bonus they do not get.
correction: Split the record. Drop the passive entry from the situational list (situational=false for that half) and record it as an engine gap instead: needsEngineWork=true, "untrained weapon strikes should use your level as the proficiency term while this ring is worn/invested — needs a per-weapon proficiency-override hook in the strike engine, not a display flag." KEEP only the activated entry as situational: "+2 circumstance (+4 if you are expert in any weapon)" / when: "once per day, free action, triggered when you make an attack with a weapon you're untrained in" / targetKind strikeAttack — that one is genuinely a triggered, typed, once-per-day circumstance bonus. If the owner prefers to keep a single informational star, this must at minimum be needsHumanDecision, because the global 'attack' target makes it read as applying to trained weapons too.

problem: Incomplete: the activated effect is omitted entirely. If you roll a success on the check, you get a critical success instead." correction: Add a second entry: bonus: "success becomes a critical success", when: "once per day, when you activate the cloak (2 actions, command) to Request something of a creature", targetKind 'skill', skill 'diplomacy'. Keep the existing +1 item / Make an Impression entry unchanged (it is correct, and the reciprocal Gather-Information-about-you clause is rightly called out as unrepresentable).

problem: Same omission as the base cloak. Verified text carries the same activation with "**Frequency** twice per day" (record's counters: max 2 per day), and the +2 item bonus half is correct.
correction: Add: bonus: "success becomes a critical success", when: "twice per day, when you activate the cloak (2 actions, command) to Request something of a creature", targetKind 'skill', skill 'diplomacy'.

problem: Same omission, and the major grade's activation is strictly stronger than the other two, so dropping it loses the most. Verified text: "**Frequency** three times per day ... If you roll a success on the check, you get a critical success instead. If you roll a critical failure on your Diplomacy check when you activate the cloak, you get a failure instead." problem: The second bonus's condition says "you spend the reaction after damaging an aberration with the sword (once per round)". The record's own text is "**Activate** ⟨4⟩ envision / **Frequency** once per round / **Trigger** You damage an aberration with the *Kortos Diamond* / **Effect** You deal an additional 2d8 damage". ⟨4⟩ is a FREE ACTION, not a reaction — confirmed by the app's own glyph table in src/sheet/RichText.tsx (GLYPH_TITLE: '4': 'Free action', '5': 'Reaction'), and by the fact that records which really are reactions (spangled-riders-suit, jawbreaker-shield) print ⟨5⟩ and carry activationCost.type === 'reaction'. Player-facing text that tells someone to spend their reaction when the ability costs a free action is a table-level error.
correction: Change the 'when' to: "free action (envision), triggered when you damage an aberration with the sword; once per round". The +2 item bonus to saves against mental effects while wielding is correct as written. Separately, note the internal inconsistency: this spec registers an activated damage rider as a strikeDamage bonus while the jawbreaker-shield spec explicitly excludes its reaction as "an action, not a stat bonus" — pick one policy for activated riders.

problem: The spec pins this record to "for 10 minutes after drinking" and its engineNote claims "This record is the combined parent entry; the separate 'greater' record carries the 8-hour duration" — implying only two records exist. core.json actually has THREE: olfactory-obfuscator (the combined parent, level 3, no price, text says "For the listed duration"), olfactory-obfuscator-lesser (level 3, 9 gp, "For 10 minutes after drinking"), and olfactory-obfuscator-greater (level 10, 225 gp, 8 hours). The 10-minute duration belongs to the -lesser record, which has its own id and was not classified.
correction: On the parent record, phrase the condition without a duration: "+4 item, for the elixir's listed duration after drinking (10 minutes lesser / 8 hours greater), against Seek attempts by creatures using only scent — no bonus if they use any other sense". Add a matching entry for olfactory-obfuscator-lesser (+4 item, 10 minutes). Also flag the policy question the same way bloodhound-mask/vaccine/addiction-suppressant parents raise it: should combined parent records be registered at all when per-grade records exist, or would that double-star the stat?

problem: The condition is broadened past what the text grants the owner. The record says "Creatures within the line gain a +1 item bonus to saving throws and Charisma-based skill checks", and the item is described as aiming "the spotlight outward from your body" (usage: mounted-on-a-tripod-or-bracket, not invested). Nothing in the text puts the activator inside the line, and a line area emanating from you does not include your own space — so the spec invents "while you are inside the spotlight's beam" for the sheet owner and stars FIVE of that owner's stats (all saves + Deception/Diplomacy/Intimidation/Performance) off an ally/area buff. This directly contradicts the same chunk's own (correct) handling of shield-of-the-unified-legion, which was marked situational:false precisely because the novel effect targets allies rather than the bearer.
correction: Either set situational:false with reasonIfNot "the +1 item bonus goes to creatures standing in the beam, not to the person aiming the spotlight — there is no target kind for another character's stats" (keeping needsEngineWork for party/ally buffs), or keep the entries but set needsHumanDecision with the question "should an area buff the owner is not normally inside star the owner's own stats?". Do not register five starred stats on the owner as currently written. The skill list itself (the four Cha-based skills) is right.

id: alcohol, bloodeye-coffee, flayleaf, blood-sap, elven-absinthe, scour, sun-orchid-poultice, vaccine, bloodhound-mask (+ -lesser/-moderate/-greater), addiction-suppressant (+ -lesser/-moderate/-greater/-major)
problem: Every one of these correctly describes in its engineNote that the bonus only exists while a drug stage / elixir duration is ACTIVE and must not be marked from mere possession — but none of them sets needsEngineWork:true. zerk and olfactory-obfuscator set the flag for the identical gap. correction: Set needsEngineWork:true on every consumable/drug record in the chunk, with the note "requires an active-effect gate (drug stage or elixir duration), not inventory possession". Uniformly, so the flag can be used as the triage filter.

problem: Two issues, both minor. (1) The record reads "While wearing a stole of civility, you receive a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks...", but neither skill entry carries the wearing gate, unlike every other worn/held item in the chunk (bullhook-greater, spangled-riders-suit, kortos-diamond, staff-of-the-black-desert all state theirs). Decide one policy for activated non-modifier effects and apply it to the stole's temp HP and sun-orchid-poultice's 20 temp HP together — either both are registered as hp entries or neither is (jawbreaker-shield's reaction was excluded).

problem: The classification (+4 item to the listed Craft subjects, +1d6 vs orcs) is correct and the engineNote rightly calls out that passiveEffects.skills.crafting = 4 over-applies a subject-restricted bonus to every Crafting check. But it misses a second, identical over-application in the same record: passiveEffects.senses grants "greater darkvision" unconditionally, while the text says "If you are a dwarf, you gain greater darkvision while holding the axe. If you are not a dwarf, you are Stupefied 4 while holding the axe" — so a non-dwarf carrying the axe currently gets free greater darkvision and none of the penalties.
correction: Extend the engineNote to cover the sense: greater darkvision is gated on being a dwarf AND holding the axe, and the non-dwarf/orc penalties (stupefied 4, drained 4, enfeebled 4) are unmodelled. Neither is expressible with the listed target kinds, so this is an engine/data note, not a new bonus entry.

problem: Encoding bug: situational is true but there is NO bonuses array, so the entry is empty. The reading itself is right ('If the animal companion already has scent, IT gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception when using scent against fiends' — the companion, not the PC), but every other other-creature case in this same batch is encoded situational:false + needsEngineWork:true (guiding-shot, shielded-recovery, area-armor, shield-from-arrows, blanket-defense, lesson-of-the-broken-wing). As written this record is inconsistent and would either produce a registry entry with nothing to display or, worse, a star on the PC with no text.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot 'The +2 circumstance bonus is to the animal companion's Perception, not the character's', and keep needsEngineWork:true + engineNote 'needs a companion-stat situational lane; conditions are doubly narrow (only when the companion uses its scent sense, and only against fiends)'.

problem: The engineNote states as settled fact that the Will-vs-fear increase is 'granted to your allies' and therefore out of reach for this sheet. That is only one reading. The base class feature it modifies (classFeatures/commanders-banner) says the aura 'gives you and all allies in a a +1 status bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects' — the commander explicitly DOES receive the base +1. Whether Glorious Banner raises the commander's own bonus to +2 is genuinely ambiguous (the same sentence's next clause switches to 'you and affected allies', which cuts the other way), so it should not be closed off with needsHumanDecision:false. The three marked bonuses (+1 status to AC / Fortitude / Reflex) are correct.
correction: Keep the three AC/Fort/Reflex entries as-is, but set needsHumanDecision:true with the question: 'Commander's Banner gives the +1 status vs fear to "you and all allies"; does Glorious Banner's increase to +2 apply to the commander's own Will saves/DCs vs fear, or literally only to allies?' Also worth recording in the note that the commander's own baseline +1 status to Will saves vs fear lives on classFeatures/commanders-banner, which the feats-only lookup can never reach.

problem: The engineNote's factual claim is false: 'this archetype's own dedication does not necessarily grant it [Warfare Lore]'. war-mage-dedication (this feat's own listed prerequisite) reads 'You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Warfare Lore. If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.' — so every character who can take Siege Ritualist is guaranteed to have Warfare Lore. problem: The engineNote's factual claim is false: 'there are two records with this id text in core.json (Player Core and Battlecry! printings) with identical wording'. There is exactly one record keyed guiding-shot, source 'Pathfinder Battlecry!' — no duplicate exists in any collection. The classification (situational:false, ally-only, 'the next creature other than you') is correct.

problem: The bonus string '+4 circumstance (the shield's Take Cover value) instead of the usual +2' hard-codes a baseline that is only right for a tower shield. In core.json tower-shield has acBonus 2 (description: 'AC increases to +4 if you are using the Take Cover action') but fortress-shield has acBonus 3, and its description gives no number at all ('Getting the higher bonus for this shield requires using the Take Cover action while the shield is raised'). The feat text itself never states any number, so 'the usual +2' is an invented constant for one of the two shields the feat names.
correction: Phrase the magnitude shield-relative, e.g. bonus: 'your raised shield's higher Take Cover AC value (tower shield: +4 instead of +2)' with the engineNote already-correct point that the number must be read off the equipped shield and REPLACES rather than stacks with the raised-shield circumstance bonus.

problem: needsEngineWork is set true on the grounds that "'speed' is not in the current SituationalTarget union". Per the target schema I was given, 'speed' IS a permitted target kind, so this is a false engine-work flag on an otherwise correct entry (the record does say "+10-foot status bonus to speed" at Stage 1). correction: Set needsEngineWork false and drop the union complaint from engineNote (keep the note that quickened / Drained 2 / Stupefied 2 are conditions, not bonuses). Separately, reword the 'when': "(1 round after you Interact to take it)" reads as a 1-round delay; the record has NO Onset line — the 1 round is the duration of Stage 1. Use "while Stage 1 is active (1 round; maximum duration 1 minute)".

problem: Same false engine-work flag: needsEngineWork true because "'speed' is not yet in the SituationalTarget union". 'speed' is a permitted kind in the schema. The bonus data itself is right — the umbrella record does say "You gain an item bonus to Athletics checks and you gain the listed status bonus to your Speed" with +2/+3/+4 and +10/+15/+20 ft in the graded blocks, and item-vs-status types are correctly distinguished.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false; keep only the substantive part of engineNote (umbrella record carries no concrete numbers; the -1 AC / -2 Reflex drawback has no slot in this schema). Also consider whether an umbrella record with a range string as its bonus ("+2 / +3 / +4 item") should be registered at all, since the three graded ids carry the real numbers.

correction: Set needsEngineWork false; retain the note about the one-size-larger rider and the -1 AC / -2 Reflex penalty.

problem: The engineNote asserts as fact that the trained-in-Survival requirement "is attached to the Calculate activity, NOT to the identify-celestial-bodies bonus". The record does not say that — it states it flatly and unqualified: "To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival." The spec's conclusion (do not bind the bonus to skill 'survival') is still right — being trained in Survival is a prerequisite, not the skill rolled — but the justification is invented and the 'when' string omits a stated requirement.
correction: Drop the "attached to the Calculate activity" claim from engineNote and add the prerequisite to the condition text: "on checks to identify celestial bodies, if you are trained in Survival (astrolabe held in two hands...)". problem: Coverage is inverted across the sovereign-steel family. The material text — "All sovereign steel items (including weapon and armor below) ... grant their bonus to saves the owner makes specifically to protect the item from magic" — explicitly names armor, yet the +4 circumstance save leg is registered ONLY on the two Sovereign Steel Object records (raw material priced per Bulk, which the spec itself doubts should ever star) and NOT on the three armor records, which are the ones a character actually wears. The +1 circumstance AC vs spell attack rolls on the armor records is correct and verified.
correction: Decide one way and apply it consistently across sovereign-steel-armor, sovereign-steel-armor-standard-grade and sovereign-steel-armor-high-grade vs sovereign-steel-object-standard-grade / -high-grade: either add the "+4 circumstance, on a save you make specifically to protect this sovereign steel item from magic (e.g. vs. rusting grasp)" leg to the armor records too, or drop it from the Object records as an unrollable/GM-side effect. Note the armor records' own description text does not repeat the +4 clause (it lives on the material record), so if the rule is strict grounding in the record's own text, the Object entries are the ones to drop.

problem: The condition is narrowed and the engineNote invents a Paizo typo that the text does not support. The record reads: 'you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge.' That is a DISJUNCTION with two qualifying branches. The spec's `when` keeps only the second branch ('if that Lore could identify it') and silently drops the first. The engineNote then asserts the first branch 'reads as a Paizo typo for "if you are trained in that Lore"' — that is an invented rewrite. The printed clause is coherent as written: Dad Joke is a lovingly tailored joke, so a Lore the TARGET is trained in (Farming Lore for a farmer) is exactly the kind of Lore you would build the pun from. Rewriting a printed condition on a typo hunch is the 'condition invented or broadened beyond what the text says' failure mode.
correction: Restore both printed branches and drop the typo claim. Use when: 'when you use Dad Joke and substitute a Lore check for the skill that would identify the target, if the target is trained in that Lore or that Lore could identify it'. Keep bonus '+2 circumstance', targetKind 'skill'. Keep needsEngineWork true, but restate the engine gap accurately: the registry keys Lore individually as `lore:*` (see the SituationalTarget doc comment in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), so there is no key meaning 'whichever Lore fits the target'; skill 'lore' is a placeholder for a missing any-Lore target. If the typo reading is still suspected, that belongs in needsHumanDecision as a question, not applied as a silent edit to the condition.

problem: The needsHumanDecision question presents only two readings and omits the most likely one, so the Acrobatics row as written is probably over-broad. Text: '+1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, Acrobatics checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone.' The spec asks only 'does the qualifier scope the Reflex half, or all three?' — but the natural third reading is that it scopes the Acrobatics AND Reflex halves and leaves only unarmed attacks unqualified, because every action in the trailing list is an Acrobatics/Reflex action (Escape can be an Acrobatics check, Grab an Edge is a Reflex save, avoiding falling prone is Acrobatics or Reflex). Under the spec's chosen reading the sheet stars ALL Acrobatics while the clothing is worn, which is a broader claim than the sentence supports. Second problem: the engineNote suggests the unarmed-attack and Acrobatics halves 'could be treated as flat item bonuses in the maths instead of stars'. Doing that for unarmed attacks would be a real bug — Handwraps of Mighty Blows already supply an ITEM bonus to unarmed attacks, item bonuses do not stack, so folding this into the maths would silently inflate the strike total for any character with handwraps.
correction: Rewrite the question to offer three readings: (a) qualifier scopes only Reflex saves/DCs; (b) qualifier scopes Acrobatics and Reflex, leaving only unarmed attacks unconditional; (c) qualifier scopes all three. Flag (b) as the reading the sentence structure best supports, and until the owner rules, scope the Acrobatics entry with when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone' rather than the bare 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing'. Delete the suggestion to move any part of this into the maths, or replace it with an explicit warning that the unarmed-attack half must stay display-only because it is an item bonus that does not stack with Handwraps of Mighty Blows.

problem: `situational: false` is being used to mean 'out of scope' rather than its defined meaning ('unconditional, so it belongs in the maths'), and the chunk applies it inconsistently. Six records whose bonus lands on someone other than the character (fear-no-pain, swift-support, bounce-boost, personalized-poisoning, guardians-deflection-swashbuckler, snap-out-of-it-marshal) are marked situational TRUE with an empty bonus list, while eight Kingmaker records with the same 'nothing lands on a character stat' shape are marked situational FALSE with an empty list. Worse, several kingdom specs contradict their own flag: aon-fortified-fiefs is false yet its engineNote says 'within that subsystem both modifiers WOULD be situational', and aon-inspiring-entertainment is false yet its engineNote says 'within that subsystem this one is clearly situational'. aon-civil-service is the same case — '+2 status bonus to New Leadership checks' is restricted to one named kingdom activity, so it is conditional, not unconditional. A downstream reader taking `situational: false` at its documented meaning would conclude these are flat bonuses.
correction: Unify the two families on one encoding. Recommended: reserve `situational: false` for genuinely unconditional bonuses, and mark every 'nothing lands on a character statistic' record as situational true + bonuses [] + needsEngineWork true, with the reason (ally-facing / companion-facing / kingdom subsystem) in engineNote. Under that rule, flip aon-civil-service, aon-cooperative-leadership, aon-crush-dissent, aon-fortified-fiefs, aon-free-and-fair, aon-insider-trading and aon-inspiring-entertainment to situational true with empty bonuses. aon-practical-magic is the one kingdom record that should stay false, because '+1 status bonus to Magic checks' really is unconditional inside its own subsystem. Either way, remove the engineNote sentences that assert the opposite of the flag on the same record.

problem: The engineNote contradicts the data it ships. It says 'the sheet must not present them as bonuses' while the two -1 circumstance penalties are placed in the `bonuses` array, which is exactly what the sheet renders as bonuses. An applier following the note would strip the penalties (losing information the player needs — Harsh Judgment penalises Seeking and Demoralizing everyone except the condemned foe) or render them under a bonus heading, the thing the note forbids. The classification itself is right: the record does read '+2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Seek your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to Demoralize them. You have a -1 circumstance penalty to Perception checks to Seek creatures other than your condemned foe...'. The live registry already carries penalty rows in the same array (barbarian-dedication: bonus "-1 (penalty)"; diverse-mystery: bonus "-1 status"), so there is precedent — the note is simply wrong about the convention.
correction: Keep all four rows and delete the contradictory sentence. Follow the existing labeling convention in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts so the display reads as a penalty rather than a bonus — e.g. bonus '-1 circumstance (penalty)' for the two Seek/Demoralize-others rows, matching barbarian-dedication's '-1 (penalty)'. Apply the identical change to the duplicate record aon-harsh-judgment, whose engineNote carries the same contradictory sentence.
